summary: The cut strip shows a back-turned character who is mostly stable but sits cropped at the right edge, and the 115.3 s spike is a hard cut to a washed-out pink shot, with a pop right before it.

faults.what: Right after the cut the character's torso, head and arm shift sideways and vertically between tiles 113.73, 113.76 and 113.79: he drops low, then rises again by 113.83, so the first frames of the shot still tween instead of landing as the shot.
faults.fix: Trim the first 4-5 frames of the shot or start the move from the settled pose so the first frame is already the shot.

faults.what: He is jammed against the right edge, with his shoulder, arm and half of his body cut off by the frame. His head is cropped at the top in 113.69-113.79. The subject is poorly framed for a character who 'knows exactly what he is doing'.
faults.fix: Pan or reframe so he sits inside the frame with room on the side he walks toward.

faults.what: The back view is stiff and symmetrical with both arms hanging. There is no skirt grab or clear intent, so the idea of taking up his skirt is not readable.
faults.fix: Add the hand lifting the skirt hem and a clear lean into the walk.

faults.what: At 115.36 the picture swaps from the dark wooden yard close-up to a heavily washed-out pink room, which is a different set and a different character scale. It reads as a blown-out flash or a wrong-shot cut, not the glide to the door. The 115.29-115.33 close-up is also whipped with heavy blur beforehand.
faults.fix: Remove the stray cut or lower the pink bloom so the door shot reads as a clean continuation of the move.

faults.what: In the pink frames he stands with a hand on his hip, looking up, with almost no movement from 115.36 to 115.53. This is a stuck, blank pose rather than gliding to the door by choice.
faults.fix: Show him moving toward the door with an eye lead and weight shift, or cut this hold.
